triggers: a kernel on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942) risks the '4. Multi-wave (4 waves) is 2.9× slower for backward despite working for forward' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942): 4. Multi-wave (4 waves) is 2.9× slower for backward despite working for forward

problem.statement: Pitfalls: FlyDSL Attention Backward dQ + dK+dV on MI308X (gfx942) -- 4. Multi-wave (4 waves) is 2.9× slower for backward despite working for forward

payload.attempted: The forward kernel uses BLOCK_SIZE=256 (4 waves) successfully. For backward, the natural assumption is that more waves = better latency hiding = better performance.
payload.lesson: Multi-wave is not universally better. For kernels with high VGPR pressure and many barriers, single-wave avoids synchronization overhead and register spilling. Always benchmark both configurations.

established_fact.mechanism: The backward kernel has more inter-wave synchronization points (3 barriers per Q-tile vs 1-2 in forward). Each barrier stalls all waves. Additionally, the backward kernel's VGPR pressure is already at 196 Accum VGPR for 1 wave; 4 waves would require each wave to fit in 512/4 = 128 VGPR total, causing massive spilling.

payload.observed: block_n=32, 4 waves: 32.0 ms vs 11.1 ms single-wave (2.9× slower).
